summary: Provides guidelines for personal interaction in the IETF. It is a Best Current Practice. It was replaced by RFC 7154.

eli5.summary: It's a list of manners for the club.

questions: what is ietf code of conduct
what are ietf guidelines for conduct
subtitle: Rules for respectful and productive interaction in the IETF.

tldr.problem: The IETF is a large, global, diverse organization where disagreements can become heated and hinder the consensus-building process.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3184 establishes four principles of conduct: respect for colleagues, impartial testing of ideas, global thinking, and preparation for meetings. These guide interactions in person, online, and in working groups.
tldr.outcome: The guidelines have become foundational to IETF culture. RFC 3184 was later updated and replaced by RFC 7154 to strengthen protections and clarify expectations.

today: RFC 3184 is a Best Current Practice that was obsoleted by RFC 7154, which strengthens and clarifies the guidelines. However, the core principles remain central to IETF culture.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: The IETF's work depends on cooperation among people with diverse backgrounds, cultures, ideas, and communication styles. RFC 3184 provides a set of guidelines for personal interaction to help participants work together effectively. The guidelines apply at IETF meetings, on mailing lists, and wherever IETF participants collaborate. If conflicts arise, they are resolved according to procedures in BCP 25.
sections.eli5: The IETF is a club where people all around the world work on Internet technology. This explains how members should treat each other.

sections.title: Principles of Conduct
sections.content: RFC 3184 outlines four core principles. First, participants extend respect and courtesy to colleagues at all times, recognizing their diverse origins and capabilities. English is the working language, but participants from non-English-speaking backgrounds deserve clear, accommodating speech. Second, ideas are tested impartially without finding fault with the person proposing them. Disagreements use reasoned argument rather than intimidation or personal attacks, following the motto: "Reduce the heat and increase the light." Third, participants think globally, seeking solutions for the entire Internet, not just specific networks, vendors, or users. Participants use their best judgment to meet the needs of diverse technical and operational environments. Fourth, individuals attending working group meetings prepare in advance by reading relevant documents and mailing list archives, respecting the limited meeting time for productive work rather than education.
sections.eli5: Be respectful. Argue ideas, not people. Think about the whole Internet. Come prepared to meetings. These four rules keep the IETF working.

sections.title: Status and Evolution
sections.content: RFC 3184 is a Best Current Practice document that codified longstanding expectations within the IETF community. It reflects the organization's commitment to creating an inclusive, technically excellent environment. The document was developed with input from Mike O'Dell, Dave Crocker, and members of the POISSON Working Group. RFC 3184 served as the primary conduct guideline for the IETF for a decade.
sections.eli5: This is an official rule book, not just a suggestion. Many people helped write it, and it was the main code of conduct for IETF members for ten years.
